landing.heroSubtitle: Upload your notes and past papers, then ask questions, practise with quizzes and plan your study time. Every answer shows where it came from.
landing.featuresTitle: Everything for your course in one place
landing.f1Body: Keep materials, notes and past papers together, one subject at a time.
landing.f2Body: Ask in English, Hindi or Gujarati and see exactly which page an answer came from.
landing.f3Body: Practise on the topics you find hard and see how you are improving.
landing.f4Body: Understand what a question asks and get feedback on your own drafts.
landing.f5Body: Study sessions are suggested around your deadlines. Nothing is added without your approval.
landing.privacyBody: Your materials are private to your account by default. You bring your own AI key, so you decide which provider sees your questions.
landing.sampleLabel: Sample preview. Illustrative only, not a real answer.
landing.sampleQuestion: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
landing.sampleAnswer: A process has its own memory space, while threads in a process share memory and run independently.

privacy.title: Privacy and AI safety
privacy.intro: Your notes and questions are sent to the AI service you chose. MindNest cleans them first.
privacy.always: Aadhaar, PAN, card numbers and secret keys are always hidden before anything is sent.
privacy.injection: Commands hidden inside documents (such as “ignore the rules”) are quoted as plain text and never followed.
privacy.output: Answers are checked before you see them: pictures from other sites, scripts and tracking links are removed.
privacy.toggle: Also hide e-mail addresses, phone numbers and UPI ids
privacy.toggleHint: Recommended. The AI sees [EMAIL] or [PHONE] instead, and your own saved messages stay unchanged.

models.title: Local retrieval models
models.intro: Two small models run on your own laptop to find the right passages in your materials: one turns text into vectors (embedding), the other puts search results in order (reranking). This page shows what the running service reports.
models.noLocalLlm: These are not chat models. MindNest does not run a language model on your laptop; answers always come from the LLM provider you set up in the other tab.
models.down: The model service is not reachable

models.problem.unsupported: This server cannot ask the service for its status. Update the API.
models.problem.bad_response: The service answered, but not in a form this page understands. Update the model service.
models.start: Start it on your laptop (the API looks for it at {service}):
models.degraded: Until it runs, search falls back to word matching only and results are less precise.
models.embedding.body: Turns your materials and your questions into vectors so similar meaning can be found, in English, Hindi and Gujarati.
models.reranker.body: Reads each candidate passage next to the question and puts the best ones first.
models.dimWarning: The service produces vectors of size {dim}, but the database expects {expected}. Search will fail until they match.
models.gpuHint.yes: The models run in half precision on the graphics card. If its memory runs out, reranking moves to the processor.
models.gpuHint.no: Without a graphics card the models run on the processor, which is slower but gives the same results.
models.usage.intro: Three search modes exist so the Evaluation Lab can compare them on the same questions. Chat uses the advanced one.
models.mode.baseline.body: Meaning search only, with the embedding model.
models.mode.hybrid.body: Meaning search and word search, merged by rank.
models.mode.advanced.body: Meaning search picks candidates, then the reranking model orders them.
models.usage.constants: Each passage is cut to {chars} characters for reranking; hybrid merging uses rank constant {k}.

evx.glossary.title: What the scores mean
evx.glossary.intro: Every score runs from 0% to 100% (MRR from 0 to 1).
evx.about.recall_at_1: How often the needed evidence is the very first passage found.
evx.about.recall_at_3: How often the needed evidence is among the first three passages found.
evx.about.recall_at_k: How much of the needed evidence is among the top K passages. The main search score.
evx.about.precision_at_k: Of the top K passages, how many actually hold the evidence. Low means a lot of noise.
evx.about.hit_at_k: How often at least one of the top K passages has the evidence.
evx.about.mrr: How high the first good passage ranks: 1 means always first, 0.5 means usually second.
evx.about.correctness: Whether the written answer agrees with the reference answer. Needs answers and AI grading.
evx.about.faithfulness: Whether every claim in the answer is backed by the passages shown. Low means it made things up.
evx.about.relevance: Whether the answer actually addresses the question that was asked.
evx.about.cited_any: How often the answer points to at least one source.
evx.about.citation_validity: How often the cited numbers match a passage that really exists in the search results.
evx.about.citation_accuracy: How often a cited passage really contains the evidence, not just any passage.
evx.about.abstain: For questions the materials cannot answer: how often it said so instead of guessing.
evx.about.false_refusal: For questions the materials can answer: how often it wrongly refused. Lower is better.
evx.about.injection_leaked: How often text hidden inside a material changed the answer. Should be 0%.
evx.runPage.scoresHint: Higher is better unless a score says otherwise.
